Hi — looping in briefly.

This is a pretty common Google Calendar quirk: if an event is created as a 'floating' event (no timezone) or forwarded across accounts with different default timezones, GCal can display a local time that doesn't match the textual time. Two quick fixes:

1) Resend the invite from the organizer account and explicitly set the timezone (e.g., Europe/London).
2) Attach a canonical .ics that includes the TZID — recipients can import that to ensure correct local mapping.

I'll generate an .ics and resend from priya@redwood.com with the organizer timezone set to GMT (Europe/London). That should stop the calendar from converting the time incorrectly.

Also, Tom, if you're using the new Calendar UI, double-check Settings > Time zone and uncheck "Ask to update primary time zone" if you want fixed mapping.

—Aditya
